body.statement: For all \(G\equiv_E H\) and \(e\in E(H)\setminus E(G)\), \(G+e\equiv_E G\) for every \(e\in U_{\to}\cup U_{\leftrightarrow}\). This includes SCC-changing arrows, directed self-loops, unordered bidirected loops \(\{u,u\}\), arbitrary directed cycles, and bidirected additions outside occupied SCC rectangles.
body.justification: This local theorem resolves the global conjecture by iteration.
body.gap: No published E-result covers these unrestricted regimes.
body.consumer: Equivalent representatives become connected by safe edge additions.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove that every profile-changing edge appearing in an E-equivalent comparison graph is individually safe to add to the base graph.
obligation.obstruction: The fixed-profile splice proves safety only for edges already generated by the directed-path and occupied-rectangle supports of the base graph.  E-equivalence alone has not been converted into the local marked replacement required for the remaining edges.
obligation.attempted: Antitonicity, first-new-edge minimality, and symmetric comparison through the union were combined with singleton composition.  They reduce the issue to the contextual replacement obligation but do not force a compatible replacement walk.  Both prescribed sparse exhaustive gates passed without producing a falsifying witness.
obligation.partial_result: The theorem holds whenever \(e\in E(\Gamma(G))\setminus E(G)\): the proved replacement gives \(\mathcal I_E(G+e)=\mathcal I_E(G)\).  Equivalently, \(G+e\) lies in the interval between the E-equivalent graphs \(G\) and \(\Gamma(G)\).  This includes all fixed-profile additions and both traversal orientations of every affected lifted edge, but not the unrestricted profile-changing cases quantified in the target.
